Admissions FAQ
How do I get a printed copy of the Graduate Catalog?
We no longer print a paper copy of the catalog. The on-line version of the graduate catalog is updated frequently and is more current than the printed version.
What are the dates for admissions deadlines?
Contact the specific graduate group for further information on the admissions process in that group. Applicants are advised that deadlines are program specific and start on December 8 for PhD consideration. Please be sure to check the Admissions Calendar or reach out to your specific program of interest to confirm the deadline.
Where should GRE and TOEFL scores be sent? Do you accept IELTS in lieu of TOEFL?
There are several programs that no longer require GRE scores. Please check the individual program website for details. If they are required, the scores should be sent to the Graduate Division of Arts and Sciences office electronically through ETS. The school code is 2926. GRE scores are valid for 5 years and TOEFL scores for 2 years.
IELTS scores are accepted in lieu of the TOEFL. You should arrange for IELTS to send the score directly to us and we will manually attach it to your application.
I am applying from abroad. What form of payment should I use for my application fee?
In payment of the application fee, applicants should use a credit card. All major cards are accepted. See the payment page of the on-line application for further details.
I am not a United States citizen. How do I get a visa?
Upon admission, after accepting your offer and paying the enrollment fee, your name will be forwarded to the University's International Student and Scholar Services. They will provide you with a link to their database once your acceptance has been received. All documents required for the visa process will be issued by their office. Any questions regarding the visa process should be directed to them.
Where can I access the Campus Safety and Security brochure?
To review the University's most recent annual report containing this information, please go to the current brochure.
I've been admitted! What should I do next?
Congratulations!
You will be sent an email that a decision has been reached. Sign into your application portal and click on the 'decision has been made' link. Click on the link embedded in the letter to record your decision. If you accept the offer, you will be required to pay a non-refundable enrollment fee, by credit card.
You must also send an official copy of your final transcript, including degree conferral, to this office. You may also have the final transcript sent electronically by your home institution to the sas-gradadmissions@sas.upenn.edu address.
Once you complete these steps, visit our New Student Page for a checklist of things to do before your arrival!
How do I send my official transcripts?
Once you have accepted your offer, you will be required to provide official final transcripts of all previous academic work to verify the information provided. Transcripts submitted directly by students are not considered official.
In order for a transcript to be considered official, we require one of the following:
Emailed transcript from official electronic delivery service or issuing institution. Official transcripts must be sent electronically to sas-gradadmissions@sas.upenn.edu. If there is no option to select The University of Pennsylvania Graduate Division of Arts and Sciences, you must check "other" or "alternate" and enter the email address above.**
Original hard copy mailed to the Graduate Division directly from the issuing institution in a sealed envelope bearing the institution's stamp or seal to the address below:
Graduate Division
School of Arts and Sciences
University of Pennsylvania
3401 Walnut Street, Suite 322A
Philadelphia, PA 19104-6228
We strongly encourage the use of electronic delivery services whenever possible. Physical mail may be subject to carrier delays or disruptions that may impact the timely receipt of your documents.
**Transcripts sent to the general University of Pennsylvania email address or to the Undergraduate Office will not be accessible to the Graduate Division Office, and we will not receive the transcript.
I accepted my offer, how do I get my PennID?
Accepted graduate students receive their 8-digit PennID number directly from Penn Information Systems and Computing (ISC). This number is assigned via email shortly after you officially accept your offer of admission through the online application portal.
If you have not received your PennID within 48-72 hours after accepting your offer, first check your spam/junk folder, then contact your department's Graduate Coordinator if you still cannot locate PennID.
How do I set up my PennKey?
Penn ISC automatically emails set up codes with instructions to incoming students. You will receive an email sent to the email address you used when you applied.
If you didn't receive a set up code, please check your junk and spam folders. If you still cannot locate the code you will need to contact PennKey Support for assistance.
I’ve set up my PennKey, how do I activate my student email?
As an SAS Graduate student, you will create an email address based on your PennKey. For example, if your PennKey is "bfranklin", your email address will be " bfranklin@sas.upenn.edu ". This is the address that is entered for you in the Penn directory and is the address that your professors, advisors and others at Penn will use to communicate with you.
For instructions on setting up your student email, please visit SAS Computing’s Getting Started with SAS Student Email webpage.
Please note that you need to wait at least 24 hours after registering your new PennKey before you can create your SAS email address.
